post.headline: Set up message encryption during onboarding
post.subtext: Recipients can search Proton Mail for a key or paste a public PGP key before sources begin using the tip line.

social.linkedin:
People setting up a tip line need encryption in place before they ask sources to use it.

In Hush Line onboarding, recipients can add a public encryption key by searching Proton Mail or pasting a PGP public key manually. That setup keeps the first disclosure workflow focused: sources do not need an account, and recipients have a key ready for protected message delivery.

Sign up at https://hushline.app.

post.rationale: Chose the onboarding encryption screenshot because it is the least repetitive candidate in the shortlist. The settings encryption screen repeats the recent settings encryption angle more directly, and the email validation screen repeats an exact content key from 2026-05-08. This post is written for recipients and staff preparing a tip line, grounded in the documented workflow of adding encryption before publishing a public intake channel.
